spec.description: Returns a list of trades on the spot exchange. If no filter parameters are specified, the last 1000 trades for all pairs are received.

symbol.description: Filter the results to the currency pair.

from_ts.description: Filter the results to include the trades after this timestamp.

to_ts.description: Filter the results to include the trades before or at this timestamp.

count.description: The maximum number of trades to return.

response.title: PostTradeResult
response.description: A list of executed trades in ascending timestamp order.

last_ts.description: Timestamp of the latest trade in the list, or an empty string when the result contains no trades. Can be used as the `from_ts` parameter when requesting the next batch of trades.

anyOf.description: Timestamp of the latest trade in the list.
Empty when the result contains no trades.

trades.description: The trades, in ascending timestamp order.

price.description: Trade price excluding fees and commissions.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair.

description.description: The full description of the currency pair.

base_asset.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the base asset.

base_notation.description: Indicates that the quantity is expressed in nominal units.

quote_asset.description: ISO 4217 currency in which the trading price is expressed.

quote_notation.description: Indicates that the price is expressed in monetary value.

trade_venue.description: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) of the trading platform where the trade was executed.

trade_ts.description: Timestamp the trade was matched in the engine, to microsecond precision.

publication_venue.description: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) of the trading platform where the trade was published.

publication_ts.description: Timestamp the trade was published to market data streams.

notes: trade_venue/publication_venue and base_asset/quote_asset dropped upstream's non-standard `format: "ISO 10383"`/`format: "ISO 4217"` (not real JSON Schema formats) in favor of description text; every *_ts field uses the real `format: "date-time"` in place of upstream's non-standard `format: "ISO 8601"`. No `pagination` block declared: `from_ts`/`to_ts` genuinely walk a time range (ascending, `from_ts` exclusive-after / `to_ts` inclusive-before-or-at per the docs, and `last_ts` is explicitly documented as reusable as the next page's `from_ts`), which is shaped like this format's `window` strategy -- but the bounds are ISO-8601 strings, not the integers a `window` walk needs to do `end - start` arithmetic on (rule 7), and Kraken publishes no integer/epoch variant here. Left unspecced rather than forced into a strategy the format's arithmetic assumptions don't fit.

`last_ts` is `anyOf[date-time, ""]`, not a bare `date-time`: when `from_ts`/`to_ts` bound an empty result, Kraken sends `last_ts` as a literal empty string rather than omitting the key or sending `null` (confirmed live and captured in `examples/empty.*`; see `.agents/handoff/kraken-post-trade-empty-last-ts-not-parseable.md`). A bare `format: "date-time"` here rejects that real response under `validate=True`. Modeled honestly as a union rather than coercing `''` to absent in the shared `IsoConverter` -- that converter is shared by every client's `TimestampIso`/`TimestampMillis`/etc, and silently treating a malformed timestamp as `None` there would hide a genuinely malformed wire value on every other client using it.
